svg.aria-label: Brick Breaker uplift: the levels the plan redraws
svg.title: Brick Breaker uplift: the levels the plan redraws
svg.text: Brick Breaker uplift · level changes · dark palette
Each as the game has it now, in the art it has now, and as the plan redraws it, in the plan's art. The times are the game's own autopilot's.
Level 1 takes the autopilot two minutes at Relaxed, more than any of Basics but Checker. Four rows for six,
and a notch that lets the first ball through to the pocket above the wall.
The slowest of Basics at Relaxed. The lower band loses its tough bricks and becomes a true checker of gaps a
The one level the report marks: its last bricks hide over a shelf of steel. The shelf becomes four posts, so
every brick can be seen from the paddle.
The longest level of the thirty at every speed. The vault's mouth is as wide as the vault, its walls ask for
two hits where they asked for three, and the wall under it is one tough row over three plain.
Looked at, and left as they are
Its last bricks take 0:46 at Normal, the longest endgame of Tricks.
Three redraws were played: a row off the hedges, moss on one side
of each stall, and both. None shortened the endgame at every speed,
and the first lengthened it to 1:00 at Relaxed. The seeker is the
better answer to it than a redraw.
Its middle time is 0:39 and its longest 3:03, the widest spread of
the thirty. A gap in the bridge and open ends were both played:
the longest fell to 1:54 and 2:27 at Relaxed, and was still three
to five times the middle. Quick or slow by its first ball is the
level's nature and not its drawing; the plan leaves it, and lets
the stars reward the quick way.
